source_artifact.author: Richard Lynes
source_artifact.title: Prove AI Governance with Failure Cases Not Happy Paths

source_construct.description: A public test-surface formulation requiring refusal evidence, no downstream command, alternate-route closure, deterministic replay and a fresh request when conditions change.

transformation: Native AGL and Initiation Gates already require commit-time revalidation and stale-legitimacy refusal. The later public post is used only to harden the negative-effect evidence surface and alternate-path test fixture.
preserved_properties: a refusal should be testable at the actual consequence surface
alternate paths and queued retries must be observed
rejected_properties: LifeStack standing or bind terminology as c canonical vocabulary
mapping_failures: LifeStack does not define c formation, Beacon identity continuity, MOT-c custody or L4 human-anchor coupling

terminology_substitutions.reason: Uses the c corpus witness vocabulary and states a scoped evidence claim rather than a product-specific bind claim.

terminology_substitutions.local_term: current authority and grounding at consequence commit
terminology_substitutions.reason: Maps to AGL, CGAM permission and ARL without importing a parallel standing ontology.

native_antecedents: C-Governed CLI Agent Mesh permission model, 2026-05
claim_ceiling: This record acknowledges a useful later failure-test formulation. It does not state that c commit-time authority doctrine derives from LifeStack or that external terminology is adopted.
